title: Paired mutation calling and spatial transcriptomics identify cellular neighborhoods associated with the neoplastic outcome of mouse colitis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GEO series text for GSE334067 (32 Visium samples, a 4.15 GB RAW.tar) and GSE297394 (18 bulk RNA-seq samples, two xlsx count files of about 2.4 MB). The GSE334067 file list: each sample has a 10x filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 (12–23 MB), tissue_positions.csv, images and spatial_enrichment.csv. I downloaded sample GSM9779857: 3,698 in-tissue spots, and spatial_enrichment.csv has 19,355 genes with Moran's I (a per-gene spatial autocorrelation statistic), not per-spot labels. No file in the listing holds spot cluster labels, tumor annotations, mutation calls or the biopsy-to-spot map.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The Muc2 hom + ENU cohort: 5 mice, 16 Visium slides. 288 biopsies of 2 mm with amplicon sequencing on a 22-gene panel. Mutation calls are in Supplementary Tables 5–6, which I could not retrieve (the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint timed out). Spot clusters came from Seurat/Harmony clustering of the expression data. Raw amplicon reads are in SRA PRJNA1366784.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: GEO files are public. Per-sample h5 matrices download without a login. The supplementary mutation tables could not be retrieved.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in the files: no deposited file has a per-spot label (cluster, tumor or mutation). Per-biopsy mutation calls (Supplementary Tables 5–6, if they are per biopsy) would have to be matched to spots through a biopsy grid that isn't deposited. So the label has to be constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Checked: per-spot gene count matrices and spot coordinates are present for all 32 samples.

a4_units_stated.note: Raw UMI (unique molecular identifier) counts in a standard 10x format, with units implicit but standard.

a5_enough_rows.note: From the paper: the measured outcome (mutations) exists for 288 biopsies from 5 mice, under the 400-row minimum for classification. There are about 100k spots (3,698 counted in one sample × 32), but spots carry no measured label.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.6 GB of h5 matrices across 32 samples (estimated from file-list sizes)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Fits on a laptop if you skip the 4.15 GB tar and the images.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO's design text matches the paper: 5 Muc2 hom + ENU, 6 DSS+ENU, 4 Apc+ENU and 3+3 untreated mice, giving 32 GSM samples. I didn't verify per-cohort slide counts.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only spot-level labels (16 neighborhood clusters, the 'tumor cluster') come from unsupervised clustering of the same expression features, and they aren't deposited anyway. Predicting them would be circular.

existing_models.name: CalicoST (Nature Methods 2024), infers copy-number changes and clones from spatial transcriptomics
existing_models.score_and_split: Search summary reports about 86% average accuracy on 4 human colorectal liver-metastasis samples. It targets copy-number changes, not point mutations.

existing_models.name: STARCH, copy-number and clone inference from spatial transcriptomics (bioRxiv 2020)
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Search summary: requires the number of clones to be specified in advance

backbone.name: None fits directly. Spot-level Visium data could use Geneformer or scGPT (single-cell models), but they are trained on human single cells, not mouse FFPE (formalin-fixed) spots.

integration.partner_dataset: Human ulcerative colitis clonal mutation atlases (e.g. the Kakiuchi and Olafsson studies), joinable only on gene symbol via mouse-human orthologs
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Whether local expression neighborhoods predict which driver mutations expand, but the per-spot mutation link isn't deposited.

controls.positive_control: Nuclear β-catenin and Ctnnb1-mutant regions should map to the tumor cluster (from the paper)
controls.negative_control: Untreated Muc2 het mice (3 deposited samples)
controls.external_validation: DSS+ENU and Apc+ENU cohorts are in the same GEO series

honest_claim_h3: At best, with 288 biopsies from 5 mice, a model could say whether neighborhood composition near a biopsy relates to which of 22 genes is mutated there. That is a statistical association, not a predictive model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use spatial gene expression around a colon biopsy to predict which cancer-related mutations that biopsy carries in inflamed mouse colon.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene counts from Visium spots (each spot is a roughly crypt-sized tissue patch) overlying each 2 mm biopsy. The paper reports 288 biopsies; I didn't verify this.
plain_idea.predict: Presence of mutations in 22 colitis/cancer genes per biopsy, from targeted amplicon sequencing. These calls sit in supplementary tables I couldn't retrieve, and the biopsy-to-spot map isn't deposited.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: IBD (inflammatory bowel disease) surveillance researchers would learn whether tissue state flags pro-cancer clones. But n is too small, and the link between spots and biopsies is missing.

ml_idea: Predict per-biopsy driver mutations from neighboring Visium expression. This is not feasible: the label isn't linked to spots in the deposited files, and only 288 biopsies come from 5 mice.

effort.compute_note: Working set estimated from GEO file-list sizes of the 32 filtered h5 matrices. Nothing was timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open Supplementary Table 5 and check for per-biopsy coordinates that map onto Visium spot coordinates. If there are none, the label can't be built.

verdict_reason: Fails A2/A5/A8. The deposited Visium data has no per-spot labels. Mutation calls cover only 288 biopsies from 5 mice, with no deposited map to spots. The spot clusters themselves come from the expression features.
